intro: This branch uses the new proof skills on the simplest shapes: segments, angles and lines. The learner proves facts about angles that were only measured or noticed in earlier eras.

V.2.01.what: Working with line segments and their midpoints (the point exactly halfway), using basic rules about how lengths add up.

levels.a: Finds a whole length from its two parts when a point sits between the ends.
levels.b: Uses a midpoint to find a whole length from half of it.
levels.c: Solves for x when a midpoint splits a segment into two equal expressions, giving reasons for each step.
levels.d: Finds the midpoint of a segment from its endpoints' coordinates on a grid.

V.2.02.what: Working with angles and angle bisectors (lines that split an angle into two equal halves).

levels.a: Finds a whole angle from its two parts.
levels.b: Uses a bisector to find a whole angle from half, or puts the steps of a short proof in order.
levels.c: Solves for x when a bisector splits an angle into two equal expressions.
levels.d: Uses the fact that angles along a straight line add to 180 degrees.
levels.e: Finds an angle when a bisector and one extra ray split a larger angle.
levels.f: Finds the angle between two bisectors in a fan of four rays.

V.2.03.what: Proving facts about pairs of angles, such as why the opposite angles made by two crossing lines are always equal.

levels.a: Finds the angles made where two lines cross, using that opposite angles are equal.
levels.b: Uses that two angles adding to 180 degrees with the same angle are equal, then solves for x.
levels.c: Uses the same idea with angles that add to 90 degrees.
levels.d: Puts the steps of a short proof about angle pairs in order.

V.2.04.what: Proving angle facts when a line crosses two parallel lines (lines that never meet), such as which angles are equal.

levels.a: Spots which angles match in position when a line crosses two parallel lines.
levels.b: Finds x using equal 'Z-shaped' angles, or finds the mistaken step in a proof of that fact.
levels.c: Finds x using angles on the same side that add to 180 degrees, or finds a proof's mistake.
levels.d: Solves for x using any of these angle pairs.
levels.e: Adds a helpful parallel line through an outside point to find an angle.
levels.f: Finds the angle at a corner of a zigzag path between two parallel lines.

V.2.05.what: Working the other way: using angle measurements to prove that two lines must be parallel.

levels.a: Finds the value that makes two lines parallel, or decides whether they are.
levels.b: Picks which angle fact alone would prove two lines parallel.
levels.c: Puts the steps of a short proof that two lines are parallel in order.
levels.d: Uses the fact that two lines parallel to the same line are parallel to each other.

V.2.06.what: Proving facts about perpendicular lines, which meet at a right angle (a square corner).

levels.a: Uses right angles at perpendicular lines to find a nearby angle.
levels.b: Uses that a line perpendicular to one of two parallel lines is perpendicular to both.
levels.c: Finds the shortest distance from a point to a straight line on a grid.
levels.d: Finds the mistaken step, or the missing reason, in a proof about perpendicular lines.
